description: This figure group consists of a single rendered table (no plots, micrographs or schematics). The table, headed "Specimens | SFP/ × 10⁻⁴ | ε²₅₀/ × 10⁻⁵ | SFE/mJ·m⁻²", tabulates three calculated/derived parameters for four intercritical quenching-annealing (QA) conditions of the Fe–9Mn–5Al-0.3C (wt.%) low-density δ-TRIP steel plate: QA-620, QA-680, QA-740 and QA-800 (the numbers denote annealing temperature). All entries carry the approximation tilde. Row by row: QA-620 — SFP ~5.83, ε²₅₀ ~11.68, SFE ~36.50 mJ·m⁻²; QA-680 — ~5.98, ~12.33, ~38.27 mJ·m⁻²; QA-740 — ~5.89, ~10.76, ~33.29 mJ·m⁻²; QA-800 — ~5.59, ~9.68, ~31.53 mJ·m⁻². The table shows that all three quantities are non-monotonic in annealing temperature: they rise from QA-620 to a maximum at QA-680 and then fall steadily to the lowest values at QA-800, so the computed SFE tracks both the stacking-fault probability (SFP) and the ε²₅₀ parameter, with QA-680 giving the highest stacking-fault energy and QA-800 the lowest. No axis, scale bar or error bar exists; the caption states the values are calculated. Each QA specimen label is also the sample identifier used in the companion microstructural and tensile figures of the same study.

subfigures.description: Single four-column, four-row data table. Columns: Specimens; SFP/ × 10⁻⁴; ε²₅₀/ × 10⁻⁵; SFE/mJ·m⁻². Rows QA-620 (~5.83, ~11.68, ~36.50), QA-680 (~5.98, ~12.33, ~38.27), QA-740 (~5.89, ~10.76, ~33.29), QA-800 (~5.59, ~9.68, ~31.53). All values printed with a leading tilde.

observations.observation: The figure is a single data table, not a plot: it lists four specimen conditions in the first column (QA-620, QA-680, QA-740, QA-800) against three numeric columns headed SFP/ × 10⁻⁴, ε²₅₀/ × 10⁻⁵ and SFE/mJ·m⁻².
SFP values printed are ~5.83 for QA-620, ~5.98 for QA-680, ~5.89 for QA-740 and ~5.59 for QA-800, i.e. approximately 5.6-6.0 × 10⁻⁴ with a maximum at QA-680.
ε²₅₀ values printed are ~11.68 for QA-620, ~12.33 for QA-680, ~10.76 for QA-740 and ~9.68 for QA-800 (× 10⁻⁵), highest at QA-680 and lowest at QA-800.
SFE values printed are ~36.50 mJ·m⁻² (QA-620), ~38.27 mJ·m⁻² (QA-680), ~33.29 mJ·m⁻² (QA-740) and ~31.53 mJ·m⁻² (QA-800).
All three tabulated quantities show the same non-monotonic trend: they increase from QA-620 to a maximum at QA-680 and then decrease monotonically through QA-740 to QA-800.
Every numeric entry in the table is prefixed with a tilde, indicating the values are approximate or calculated rather than directly measured.
The caption states the table reports the 'Calculated SFE of QA specimens and some parameters'.
The caption writes the second numeric column as 'ε250/ × 10-5', which matches the pixel label ε²₅₀/ × 10⁻⁵ read as ε with subscript 50 and superscript 2.

The paper abstract states the steel is Fe–9Mn–5Al-0.3C (wt.%) processed by intercritical quenching-annealing, so the QA-620/680/740/800 labels denote the annealing temperature conditions of that steel.
